business_problem: ASAP Log needed a modern logistics data platform after relational databases could not handle the web traffic, concurrent usage, and strict SLA demands of its rapidly growing delivery network.
solution_summary: ASAP Log standardized on MongoDB Atlas to run the order-management and logistics applications behind its Brazilian delivery business after relational databases failed during early traffic testing. MongoDB now underpins 23 applications and third-party integrations, including the order system that connects vendors to a pool of 200,000 delivery drivers and handles 100,000 orders per minute. After moving from MongoDB Community to Atlas in 2022, the company used Customer Success guidance, health checks, and AWS-aligned best practices to complete the migration in two months and retire more than 40 virtual machines. Atlas Analytics Nodes now support reporting queries without impacting the production system, while autoscaling, point-in-time backup, and high availability let the team keep customer-facing services online around the clock. The Atlas-based architecture also gives ASAP Log a cleaner path to multi-cloud operations as it expands across more tools and business units.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs ASAP Log’s core logistics and order-management applications and provides the managed multi-cloud database foundation for the business.

solution_components.name: Atlas Analytics Nodes
solution_components.role: Handles reporting and analytical queries so production delivery workloads are not slowed by operational reporting.

data_flow: Vendor orders, courier activity, and delivery updates are stored in MongoDB Atlas, operational services read and write that data in real time, and Atlas Analytics Nodes serve reporting workloads without affecting the core logistics system.
business_outcome: ASAP Log improved uptime, cut infrastructure cost, retired large amounts of legacy infrastructure, and created a zero-maintenance platform that can keep scaling with order volume and new tools.
